piles.label: Thranduil's pile
piles.intro: Cards that fit Thranduil's Elves-and-graveyard deck better. Thranduil borrows the activated abilities of Elf cards in your graveyard and loots whenever a legendary Elf enters, so a non-Elf card has to beat an Elf for its slot.

piles.label: Glarb's pile
piles.intro: Cards that fit Glarb's draw-to-mill deck better. Every draw mills the opponent, Bruvac and The Water Crystal multiply it, and Glarb casts mana value 4+ straight off the top.

piles.label: Either deck
piles.intro: Cards that work in both decks: shared removal, ramp and fixing, scry Elves, planeswalkers. Copies are shared in Arena, so one card can sit in both lists.

piles.label: Fits neither
piles.intro: Cards that fit neither deck, each with the reason. Listed so nothing is silently dropped.

Legolas, Counter of Kills.text: **Thranduil:** A legendary Elf, so entering loots, but it has no activated ability to lend from the yard and no other synergy. **Glarb:** Its untap is on SCRY and the deck surveils; only Princess Yue scries.

Tam, Observant Sequencer // Deep Sight.text: Landfall prepares Tam; a prepared Tam casts a copy of Deep Sight for {G}{U}: draw a card, gain 1. **Thranduil:** Two mana a draw on a body with no graveyard tie. **Glarb:** Each copy's draw mills through Psychic Corrosion and the Tutelages, and Glarb's land plays off the top keep it prepared; small but on-plan.

Elrond, Master of Healing.text: **Thranduil:** A legendary Elf entering loots through Thranduil, but its own text needs scry and the list scries never (only surveil), and it has no activated ability for the yard. **Glarb:** "Whenever you scry" — Glarb SURVEILS; only Princess Yue scries, and the deck has few creatures to put counters on.

Ezuri, Stalker of Spheres.text: **Thranduil:** Pay {3} to proliferate twice on entry across 7 planeswalkers and Marwyn/Dionus/Kotis counters, then draws on every proliferate from High Perfect Morcant, Vraska and Yawgmoth's discard; a legendary Elf, so a Thranduil loot too. **Glarb:** The ETB adds loyalty to 9 walkers and draws two (each milling), but nothing here proliferates again.

Jyoti, Moag Ancient.text: **Thranduil:** Needs commander recasts and land creatures; only Wrenn and Realmbreaker animates a land. **Glarb:** Nothing in the list uses it.

Kiora, the Crashing Wave.text: **Thranduil:** −1 draw plus an extra land (a landfall token off Sindarin Liege); generic beside the deck's graveyard engines. **Glarb:** −1 draw mills through Corrosion and the Tutelages, +1 neutralises one threat, and the −5 Kraken emblem closes long games.

Nael, Avizoa Aeronaut.text: **Thranduil:** Sultai lands reach at most 3 basic types, so "if there are five … draw a card" never happens; it is a legendary Elf loot on a 4-mana flier with combat card selection. **Glarb:** Same dead draw; combat-gated.

Rashmi, Eternities Crafter.text: "Whenever you cast your first spell each turn, reveal the top card … cast it … If you don't, put it into your hand." **Thranduil:** A card every turn, and as a legendary Elf it loots on entry. **Glarb:** Same card a turn, and Glarb shows the top, but the card is not drawn, so nothing mills.

Imoti, Celebrant of Bounty.text: **Thranduil:** Cascade on itself plus 8 cards at MV 6+; a random free spell, not an engine. **Glarb:** Glarb casts it off the top (MV 5) and the cascade usually hits something useful, but only 7 cards here are MV 6+, so the ongoing half rarely fires.

Kruphix, God of Horizons.text: "You have no maximum hand size." **Thranduil:** No hand-size problem and rarely a creature. **Glarb:** Keeps Jin-Gitaxias's seven and feeds the Water Crystal's hand count, but Reed Richards already gives no maximum hand size.

Roalesk, Apex Hybrid.text: A counters card. **Thranduil:** Proliferate twice on death reaches five planeswalkers and Marwyn's counters, and Yarok doubles its ETB, but no graveyard role. **Glarb:** Nine planeswalkers like the death trigger, but GGU on a splash and nothing to do with draws or mill.

Tamiyo, Compleated Sage.text: "−X: Exile target nonland permanent card with mana value X from your graveyard. Create a token that's a copy." **Thranduil:** Plenty of non-Elf targets at MV ≤5 (Cloud of Darkness, Sheoldred's edict, Overlord, Yarok); the exile triggers Teval and Roots. Skip Elf targets (G-42). **Glarb:** Little in your own yard; the +1 tap is tempo.

Tawnos, the Toymaker.text: **Thranduil:** Copies Beasts/Birds; the list runs neither. **Glarb:** One Bird (Birds of Paradise).

Oko, the Trickster.text: **Thranduil:** Six mana for +1/+1 counters and a copy; no graveyard, mana or card tie. **Glarb:** Same: no draw, mill or real interaction.

Bonny Pall, Clearcutter.text: **Thranduil:** "Whenever you attack, draw a card, then … put a land card from your hand or graveyard onto the battlefield" — draw plus lands back from a yard the self-mill fills (Sidisi, Trystan, Wrenn and Realmbreaker's −2), and each land feeds Sindarin Liege's landfall tokens. The 6-mana UU cost holds it back. **Glarb:** Beau attacks each turn, so each attack draws (mills 2+); a 6-drop Glarb can cast off the top.

Omega, Heartless Evolution.text: **Thranduil:** 7 mana; X = nonbasic lands (21 in the list), so the stun locks one permanent for many turns, but it is one target. **Glarb:** Same with 22 nonbasics, and Glarb can cast it off the top; still one target for 7.

Tishana, Voice of Thunder.text: **Thranduil:** "Draw a card for each creature you control" — the wide Elf board makes it 5+, Yarok doubles it and Kinnan can put it into play from the top. **Glarb:** Usually 2–4 creatures here, each draw milling two; 7 mana that Glarb can cast off the top.

Kotis, Sibsig Champion.text: **Thranduil:** In the list: a creature cast from the yard each turn by "exiling three other cards"; lands and non-Elf spells make up most of the yard, so the cost can spare the Elf tools (G-42), and the recasts trigger Insidious Roots and Teval. **Glarb:** Own-yard recursion is not the plan.

Leovold, Emissary of Trest.text: In Thranduil's list. **Thranduil:** A 3-mana legendary Elf (a loot), a draw lock on the opponent, and a draw when targeted. **Glarb:** "Each opponent can't draw more than one card each turn" switches off the opponent's half of Dictate of Kruphix and Jace's −7, which the list runs to empty their library; it fights the mill.

Nashi, Moon's Legacy.text: "exile up to one target legendary or Rat card from your graveyard and copy it." **Thranduil:** 23 non-Elf legendary nonland cards against 15 Elves (Vile Offering, Kamahl's Vow, the walkers, Yarok, Sidisi), so the G-42 cost is avoidable; the exile triggers Teval, Oasis and Roots. Not in the list. **Glarb:** Must attack in a control deck, and its own yard holds few legends.

Nashi, Illusion Gadgeteer.text: **Thranduil:** Recursion that leaves the original in Thranduil's yard, so no G-42 cost; Yarok doubles the ETB into two cards. **Glarb:** The duplicate gains flash, so a spent Counterspell, removal spell or Traumatize comes back at instant speed.

Kotis, the Fangkeeper.text: **Thranduil:** Not Kotis, Sibsig Champion (in the list): this one exiles the OPPONENT's library on combat damage, which the deck does not care about, on a small non-Elf body no lord pumps. **Glarb:** Library exile and free casts, but only as much as its small power connects; an aggressive card in a deck that wins by milling.

Sidisi, Brood Tyrant.text: **Thranduil:** In the list: mills three on entry (six with Yarok) and attack, and most mills make a 2/2 Zombie with 45 creatures. The Zombies feed Yawgmoth's sac-draw, Insidious Roots mana, Eladamri's tap cost and Circle of Dreams. **Glarb:** Mills its own library; off-plan.

Gonti, Canny Acquisitor.text: "Whenever one or more creatures you control deal combat damage to a player" — steal their top card. **Thranduil:** The go-wide board connects, but stolen cards feed neither the yard nor Thranduil. **Glarb:** A control deck with few attackers; Gonti must connect itself, and the theft is not a draw.

Brokkos, Apex of Forever.text: **Thranduil:** A recast from the yard triggers Teval, Oasis of Renewal and Insidious Roots, and mutating onto an Elf keeps its tap ability. A mutate cast does not ENTER, so Kotis only rewards a normal Kotis or Muldrotha cast. **Glarb:** A trample threat with {G}{G} mutate on a green splash; the deck wins by mill, not combat.

Maralen, Fae Ascendant.text: **Thranduil:** In the list. Every Elf entering (33 Elves plus tokens) exiles two of their library, and the free cast is capped by the Elf count, which this deck keeps high. **Glarb:** Only Paradise Druid is an Elf, so it fires once or twice; the notes park it as a separate Elf variant.

Yarok, the Desecrated.text: **Thranduil:** In the list: "that ability triggers an additional time" — each legendary Elf entering is two Thranduil loots, and the ETB mills (Lluwen, Trystan, Sidisi, Overlord, Eulogist), Morcant's blight and Sindarin Liege's landfall tokens all double. **Glarb:** Doubles Ruin Crab's landfall (mill 6, 12 with Bruvac), Sphinx Mindbreaker and Teferi's Tutelage's loot.

Sin, Spira's Punishment.text: **Thranduil:** Per the owner's exception, an exiled Elf's ability moves to the token copy; a land hit is a free tapped land and repeats. The costs are 7 mana and randomly taking a Kotis/Muldrotha recast target. **Glarb:** The yard holds only what Glarb surveils.

Mimeoplasm, Revered One.text: **Thranduil:** "Exile up to X creature cards from your graveyard" — you choose them, but they are the same creature cards Kotis, Muldrotha and Thranduil want. **Glarb:** Own-yard creatures are not the plan.

Glamdring, Foe-hammer // Gleam of Death.text: **Thranduil:** Gleam mills six as fuel, but only ~7 instants/sorceries return and the Equipment wants a spells deck. **Glarb:** Mills your own library; the Equipment discount scales with a power the deck does not have.

Fblthp, Impossibly Lost.text: **Thranduil:** Any creature connecting on our turn draws two, and the wide Elf board connects often; but Fblthp then shuffles himself away, so it is a one-shot. **Glarb:** Rarely attacks; a one-shot draw two needing combat damage.

Goldberry, River-Daughter.text: **Thranduil:** Can shuttle Marwyn's, Dionus's or Kotis's +1/+1 counters to draw, but it costs two taps and {U} per card. **Glarb:** Only loyalty counters to move; a slow draw.

Jace Reawakened.text: "+1: Draw a card, then discard a card." (not castable before turn four) **Thranduil:** A {U}{U} loot every turn that bins an Elf for Thranduil; card-neutral, and Thranduil already loots. **Glarb:** Each loot is a draw that mills via Psychic Corrosion and the Tutelages, and each draw adds Teferi loyalty.

Katara, Waterbending Master.text: **Thranduil:** A combat-gated loot on a 2-drop that needs instant-speed casting. **Glarb:** Has the instants, but the loot needs Katara to attack.

Marit Lage's Slumber.text: Needs ten snow permanents. **Thranduil:** No snow lands or permanents. **Glarb:** Same.

Mystic Reflection.text: **Thranduil:** Copies a nonlegendary creature — its targets are the mana Elves — onto only the creatures entering next that turn; a cute token line, not an engine. **Glarb:** Few creatures enter in a draw-mill control list; off-plan.

Malcolm, Alluring Scoundrel.text: **Thranduil:** On a 2-power flier the loot is combat-gated, so it is situational. **Glarb:** The loot is a draw that mills via the Tutelages, but the list rarely attacks.

Naban, Dean of Iteration.text: **Thranduil:** No Wizards in the list. **Glarb:** Glarb is the list's only Wizard; nothing to double.

Proft's Eidetic Memory.text: **Thranduil:** A cantrip. **Glarb:** A 2-mana cantrip whose no-maximum-hand-size line matters in a heavy draw deck; the counters do nothing here.

Rona, Herald of Invasion // Rona, Tolari.text: **Thranduil:** A 2-mana loot that untaps on each of 38 legendary spells, filling Thranduil's yard several times a turn; Elrond draws off the activation and Ioreth untaps it. Card-neutral, so not ★★★. **Glarb:** Each loot draw mills through Corrosion and both Tutelages, and 26 legendary spells untap it.

The Key to the Vault.text: **Thranduil:** Combat damage looks at that many cards from YOUR library and casts one free; menace and fliers connect, but it is equip-and-attack. **Glarb:** Same, and the list has few attackers; Glarb already casts big spells off the top.

Vnwxt, Verbose Host.text: Speed rises only on your turns when an opponent loses life; max speed doubles every draw. **Thranduil:** Combat and the drains (Dawnhand Eulogist, Deathrite, Trystan) reach it, then a Thranduil loot draws four. **Glarb:** Doubled draws are doubled mill triggers, but the control list rarely makes them lose life on its own turn.

Arni, Humble Scribe.text: **Thranduil:** `{T}: Draw a card, then discard a card`, untapped by each of 45 creatures' nontoken entries — a repeatable loot that bins Elves for Thranduil, and each activation triggers Elrond's draw. A real add candidate. **Glarb:** Every loot draw triggers Corrosion and both Tutelages (mill 6, doubled by Bruvac); a Wizard for Wizard's Retort; only ~20 creatures to untap it.

Chandra, Chill of Compliance.text: **Thranduil:** +1 surveil 1 bins an Elf for Thranduil each turn, but a {1}{U}{U} walker in the deck's thinnest colour adds little beside its self-mill. **Glarb:** On the bench, screened KEY. +1 surveil feeds Matoya and Proft and returns a binned noncreature spell; the other +1 adds mana for noncreature spells; −X stuns a threat.

Callaphe, Beloved of the Sea.text: **Thranduil:** A {1}{U}{U} body whose power is blue devotion, which this G/B-heavy list barely has; the targeting tax is mild protection. **Glarb:** More devotion here, but still a ward-style tax with no draw, mill or interaction.

Elrond, Lord of Rivendell.text: **Thranduil:** A 3-mana legendary Elf (a loot on entry); scry 1 per creature entering is modest, and with no activated ability it lends Thranduil nothing from the yard. **Glarb:** Each scry is a Matoya draw, but the list has only 20 creatures, so it hinges on Matoya.

Elrond, Moon-Reader.text: "Whenever you activate an ability of a creature, draw a card" (once a turn). **Thranduil:** In the list. Tapping any of ~13 mana creatures is an activation, so it draws every turn, on the opponent's turn too; a legendary Elf (loot on entry). **Glarb:** Not in the list, but Glarb's surveil tap, Princess Yue's scry and Doctor Doom trigger it, so each turn is a draw that mills. A good add.

Fblthp, Lost on the Range.text: "You may plot nonland cards from the top of your library." **Thranduil:** {1}{U}{U} in a green-heavy list; Eladamri already casts creatures from the top. **Glarb:** Complements Glarb rather than duplicating it — it reaches the MV 3-or-less counters, Tutelages and 2-mana removal Glarb cannot cast from the top — but plotting is not a draw, so it feeds none of the mill triggers.

Geralf, the Fleshwright.text: **Thranduil:** "Other than your first spell that turn" — the mana Elves make two spells a turn reachable, and Zombies feed Yawgmoth and Insidious Roots, but it is a token engine bolted on. **Glarb:** A control deck casts most spells on the opponent's turn; few triggers.

Graviton, Fundamental Force.text: "Whenever you draw your second card each turn" — tap a creature. **Thranduil:** A loot reaches it, but a one-creature tap is minor. **Glarb:** Draws twice most turns, but a tap on the opponent's turn needs a second draw before combat (Theorist plus Notion Thief or Rhystic); M.O.D.O.K.'s edict does the job better.

Impossible Man.text: **Thranduil:** `{2}{U}`: copy Thranduil (keeping its own name, so no legend rule) for a second set of borrowed Elf abilities, or copy a mana Elf — real but mana-hungry. **Glarb:** Copy Matoya or Sheoldred, the Apocalypse for a turn; situational.

Invasion of Segovia // Caetus, Sea Tyran.text: Two 1/1 Kraken tokens; the Caetus half needs the Siege defeated in combat. **Thranduil:** Tokens feed Insidious Roots, but nothing else here. **Glarb:** Convoke and untaps do not draw or mill.

Ioreth of the Healing House.text: "{T}: Untap two other target legendary creatures." **Thranduil:** In the list since 2026-11-02. Untaps Thranduil for another borrowed {T} ability each turn (past Dionus's once-a-turn untap) plus a legendary mana Elf. **Glarb:** Untaps Glarb and Doctor Doom: a second surveil 2 (Matoya draws) and a second Doom draw, each milling.

Irma, Part-Time Mutant.text: **Thranduil:** Each combat she becomes a copy of a creature you control and stays that way — a second Thranduil or Priest of Titania — but only from combat on, and she dies to removal like any 3-drop. **Glarb:** Copy Matoya or Sheoldred, the Apocalypse; same shape, fewer targets.

Katara, Bending Prodigy.text: **Thranduil:** Waterbend {6} draws by tapping creatures — slow. **Glarb:** That draw is a mill trigger, but a 3-mana body that draws for 6 is below the bar.

Kefnet the Mindful.text: "{3}{U}: Draw a card, then you may return a land you control to its owner's hand." **Thranduil:** An expensive draw sink; blue is the light colour. **Glarb:** Expensive, but instant speed and each activation is a draw that mills; Reed Richards turns the first one each turn into four.

Kira, Great Glass-Spinner.text: Counters the first spell or ability targeting each of your creatures each turn. **Thranduil:** Protection, but it also counters Ioreth's untap, Gloom Ripper's pump target and Journey to Eternity. **Glarb:** Protects Glarb from removal; a creature-light control list gains little else.

Lulu, Stern Guardian.text: "{3}{U}: Proliferate" plus a stun counter on an attacker each combat. **Thranduil:** Seven planeswalkers and Marwyn/Dionus/Kotis counters give proliferate targets, but High Perfect Morcant already proliferates for free. **Glarb:** Nine planeswalkers to tick up, and the stun protects them; still a 4-mana activation.

Lyra, Tolarian Archangel.text: **Thranduil:** A Thranduil loot plus the draw step reaches three draws, but UU for a body, not a graveyard card. **Glarb:** Three draws in a turn is common here (Dictate, Phyrexian Arena, The Theorist on their turn), so it makes a 3/3 flier most end steps — a body, though, not a draw or a mill.

Mindlink Mech.text: Copies the nonlegendary creature that crewed it. **Thranduil:** ~18 nonlegendary creatures, mostly mana Elves, so it becomes a flying Priest or Archdruid; cute, not synergy. **Glarb:** Six nonlegendary creatures and almost no reason to crew.

Mu Yanling, Sky Dancer.text: **Thranduil:** −3 for a 4/4 flier; no graveyard hook. **Glarb:** The −8 emblem makes every Island draw (mill through Corrosion), but from 2 loyalty it takes three turns of +2.

Tome of the Infinite.text: "{U}, {T}: Conjure a random card" from its spellbook. **Thranduil:** Slow random value on blue mana. **Glarb:** A card a turn, but conjuring is not a draw, so no mill triggers.

Unctus, Grand Metatect.text: Other blue creatures have "Whenever this creature becomes tapped, draw a card, then discard a card." **Thranduil:** The mana Elves are green, so only by spending {U/P} at sorcery speed. **Glarb:** Glarb's surveil tap and Princess Yue's scry become loots, two draws a turn that each mill.

Wasp, Shrinking Savior.text: **Thranduil:** Draws one per attack at best (only its own −3/−0 makes a negative power). **Glarb:** Jace, the Perfected Mind's +1 also gives −3/−0, so two cards a turn is possible; each draw mills two.

Alora, Rogue Companion.text: **Thranduil:** "…return that creature to its owner's hand" — the bounce re-buys an ETB (Keepers, Eulogist, Sidisi, Maralen, doubled by Yarok) or a legendary Elf's Thranduil loot, and the Elves make recasting cheap; still a 4-mana do-nothing body. **Glarb:** Few attackers (Kaito, Restless Reef); tempo with no mill.

Arwen's Gift.text: **Thranduil:** A one-shot scry 2, draw 2 sorcery; the deck's card advantage is repeatable (Thranduil's loot, Elrond, Moon-Reader, Yawgmoth), so this sits below the bar. **Glarb:** Draw two mills four through Corrosion and the scry draws a third off Matoya; a one-shot competing with repeatable draw.

Charix, the Raging Isle.text: "{3}: Charix gets +X/-X … where X is the number of Islands you control." **Thranduil:** Only 7 Islands (2 basics plus typed duals); a 0/17 wall with no synergy. **Glarb:** 14 Islands make it a real blocker or attacker, but damage is not the plan and it draws nothing.

Gale, Conduit of the Arcane.text: "if you cast it, return target instant or sorcery card from your graveyard to your hand." **Thranduil:** Seven instants/sorceries (four removal spells, Vow, Vile Offering, Trystan's Command); a one-shot regrowth. **Glarb:** 21 targets and Glarb can cast it from the top, but a regrowth is not a draw and triggers none of the mill engines.

God-Eternal Kefnet.text: **Thranduil:** Few instants or sorceries to reveal. **Glarb:** Glarb shows the top, so you know whether the first draw is a spell worth copying; a 4/5 flier castable off the top, but the copy fires only on that first draw.

Gandalf, Friend of the Shire.text: Its draw needs the Ring to tempt you, and neither list tempts it. **Thranduil:** Three sorceries to flash; little gained. **Glarb:** Flashing the eight sorceries (Traumatize, Damnation, the big mills) at end of turn suits control, but that is all it does.

Irenicus's Vile Duplication.text: **Thranduil:** A flying, non-legendary token copy of one of your creatures: re-buys Cloud of Darkness, Silumgar or Sheoldred's ETB (doubled by Yarok) or a second Priest of Titania, but it needs that target on board. **Glarb:** Copies Sphinx Mindbreaker (mill ten) or Sheoldred, the Apocalypse; castable off the top at MV 4. Situational in both.

Jace, the Perfected Mind.text: **Thranduil:** Not in the list; −X self-mills 3X on demand and −2 draws three once any yard has 20 cards; one strict blue pip. **Glarb:** In the list: −X is a scalable mill Bruvac doubles, and −2 draws.

Jace, Wielder of Mysteries.text: **Thranduil:** +1 can self-mill two and draw, but `{1}{U}{U}{U}` against 15 blue sources is hard. **Glarb:** +1 mills two (four with Bruvac) and its draw triggers Corrosion and both Tutelages; the empty-library win is deck-out insurance for a list that draws hard. 24 blue sources cast it. On the deck's bench.

Leader, Super-Genius.text: **Thranduil:** Each combat a creature connives and Leader adds a draw first — draw two, discard one every turn, card advantage that bins an Elf for Thranduil; UU on a light-blue base is the cost. **Glarb:** Two draws a turn are two Psychic Corrosion and Tutelage triggers, blue is the main colour, and Glarb casts it off the top.

Multiversal Recruitment.text: **Thranduil:** A nonlegendary token copy of Priest of Titania, Voice of the Woods or an ETB miller (Keepers, Sidisi), with flashback later. **Glarb:** "Create a token that's a copy of target creature you control, except it isn't legendary" — a second Bruvac quadruples every mill, a second Matoya draws twice per surveil.

Orvar, the All-Form.text: Needs instants or sorceries targeting your own permanents. **Thranduil:** Only Trystan's Command's copy mode does. **Glarb:** None do.

Taeko, the Patient Avalanche.text: **Thranduil:** Only Elrond, Moon-Reader's blink makes creatures leave without dying. **Glarb:** Only Kaito's ninjutsu returns a creature; no blink.

Tezzeret, Betrayer of Flesh.text: **Thranduil:** +1 draws two and discards two — bins Elves for Thranduil; `{2}{U}{U}`. **Glarb:** The two draws mill via the Tutelages; few artifacts.

The Clone Saga.text: **Thranduil:** Surveil 3 bins Elves for Thranduil; II copies a creature spell (the copy isn't legendary, so no extra loot). **Glarb:** Surveil 3 triggers Matoya and Proft for draws, and II can copy Sheoldred, the Apocalypse.

Tui and La, Moon and Ocean.text: "Whenever Tui and La become tapped, draw a card." **Thranduil:** Eladamri's tap-two cost and attacks tap it, and Ioreth untaps it, so it can draw; not an Elf for Dionus. **Glarb:** No tap outlet and a control deck that rarely attacks.

Urza, Lord High Artificer.text: **Thranduil:** No artifacts. **Glarb:** Six artifacts make a modest Construct, and the {5} play-free SHUFFLES the library Glarb has set up.

Vesuvan Duplimancy.text: **Thranduil:** Needs spells that target only one of your creatures; Journey to Eternity and Trystan's Command's copy mode are about all. **Glarb:** Effectively none here.

Yue, the Moon Spirit.text: Waterbend {5} casts a noncreature spell free, so it only saves mana on a 6+ card. **Thranduil:** The Elves can tap to pay it, but its noncreature top end is Trystan's Command and the 6-mana walkers. **Glarb:** Only Breach the Multiverse and Ashiok, Sculptor of Fears cost 6+.

Iymrith, Desert Doom.text: **Thranduil:** A warded flier that refills on combat damage; the deck already has repeatable draw. **Glarb:** Draws (and so mills) only on combat damage, and attacking drops its ward.

Jace, Memory Adept.text: **Thranduil:** Its 0 can target YOU: ten cards of fuel a turn for Muldrotha, Kotis and Sidisi, but {U}{U} on a G/B base. **Glarb:** In the list. 0 mills ten (twenty with Bruvac, +4 with the Water Crystal) every turn and +1 draws; two activations end most games.

Jace, Unraveler of Secrets.text: **Thranduil:** A {U}{U} 5-drop whose scry has no payoff here; the seven walkers already in the list do more. **Glarb:** +1 "Scry 1, then draw" — Matoya draws on the scry, so two draws a turn, each milling; −2 bounce is tempo. Castable off the top; close to the list.

Krang, the All-Powerful.text: **Thranduil:** No draw-triggered permanents in the list; a 5-mana 3/3. **Glarb:** "If a player drawing a card causes a triggered ability… triggers an additional time" doubles Psychic Corrosion, both Tutelages, Sheoldred, the Apocalypse, Teferi, Temporal Pilgrim and M.O.D.O.K.; Glarb casts it off the top. The strongest add on this list.

Pharaoh Rama-Tut.text: **Thranduil:** Only 19 of 64 nonland cards are noncreature, so it is a 5-mana loot that fires about once a turn at best. **Glarb:** 44 of 64 are noncreature, so it connives most turns, and each connive draw mills through Corrosion and the Tutelages; Glarb can cast it off the top.

Syr Elenora, the Discerning.text: **Thranduil:** A 5-mana body with one draw. **Glarb:** Its ETB draw is one mill trigger for 5 mana; the list's draw engines are better.

Thryx, the Sudden Storm.text: **Thranduil:** A 5-mana flash flier, `{U}{U}`. **Glarb:** 17 spells of MV 5+ cost {1} less and can't be countered, wherever cast from; a 4/5 flier.

Victor Timely, Wily Tycoon.text: **Thranduil:** Recasts one removal spell (MV ≤4) free, twice with Yarok. **Glarb:** Many targets: Glimpse the Unthinkable, Tasha's Hideous Laughter, Maddening Cacophony, Counterspell and the removal all land in its yard; a 5-drop castable off the top.

Jace, Arcane Strategist.text: **Thranduil:** Six mana with UU for a +1 draw; Ob Nixilis and Vraska, Betrayal's Sting draw for less in the colours the list runs deep. **Glarb:** Each +1 draw mills through Psychic Corrosion and the Tutelages and Glarb casts it off the top, but at 6 it trails Ob Nixilis, Teferi and Jace, Memory Adept, already in.

Kitsune, Dragon's Daughter.text: "Exchange control of two other target creatures controlled by different players." **Thranduil:** Trade a 1/1 token or dork for their best creature; Yarok doubles the trigger. **Glarb:** Same swap with a Bird or Illusion token; MV 6 casts off the top.

Pol Jamaar, Illusionist.text: **Thranduil:** "Draw a card for each creature you control of that type" — name Elf, usually 4–6 cards, and Yarok doubles it. A 6-mana flier, below Tishana, which counts every creature. **Glarb:** Its creatures share no type (8 Humans across 21 creatures), so it draws one or two.

Ruric Thar, Biomagus.text: **Thranduil:** `{4}{U}{U}` for a flier. **Glarb:** A 6-drop flier Glarb casts off the top, double prowess off many spells.

Zahid, Djinn of the Lamp.text: **Thranduil:** A 5/6 flier with no synergy and no artifacts for the alt cost. **Glarb:** Six artifacts make it a 4-mana 5/6 flier, but the deck does not win by combat.

Jin-Gitaxias, Progress Tyrant.text: "Whenever you cast an artifact, instant, or sorcery spell, copy that spell" and counter the opponent's first. **Thranduil:** ~7 instants/sorceries; little to copy. **Glarb:** 21 instants/sorceries: a second Traumatize empties a library, and the counter taxes their removal. MV 7 casts off the top.

Jadzi, Oracle of Arcavios // Journey to.text: **Thranduil:** About seven instants and sorceries for magecraft; the Journey half's land dump feeds landfall but little else. **Glarb:** Glarb can cast it off the top (mana value 8), but an 8-mana spells-matter card in a deck of ~15 instants and sorceries.

The Magic Mirror.text: **Thranduil:** Wants instants/sorceries in the yard; the list has few. **Glarb:** Draws grow every upkeep and each mills, but `{6}{U}{U}{U}` needs a full yard.

Wan Shi Tong, Librarian.text: **Thranduil:** `{X}{U}{U}` with no graveyard tie. **Glarb:** A flash flier that draws half X, and more when they search; each draw mills.

Gadwick, the Wizened.text: **Thranduil:** `{X}{U}{U}{U}` on 15 blue sources is hard to cast. **Glarb:** 24 blue sources make it castable, and draw X is X Tutelage/Corrosion mills plus a tapper for every blue spell; MV 3 from the top, so Glarb cannot cast it there.

Aphelia, Viper Whisperer.text: **Thranduil:** An attack-for-value 2-drop; snakes add bodies, not graveyard, mana or cards. **Glarb:** A control deck that rarely attacks gets nothing from it.

Reezug, the Bonecobbler.text: **Thranduil:** `{T}`: a creature card in your yard becomes an artifact you may cast this turn — recast a non-Elf (Sheoldred, Muldrotha, Sidisi) and keep its abilities; recasting an Elf takes it off Thranduil. Overlaps Kotis and Muldrotha. **Glarb:** Its own yard holds few creatures.

Splinter, the Mentor.text: **Thranduil:** Mutagen tokens when nontoken creatures leave, which Yawgmoth's sacrifices trigger; minor. Its partner text does nothing here. **Glarb:** Few creatures leave; a 2-mana menace body.

Azula, Ruthless Firebender.text: "Whenever Azula attacks, you may discard a card." **Thranduil:** A discard outlet that has to attack; Thranduil's loot and Fauna Shaman already bin cards, and the {R} it adds is spent only in combat. **Glarb:** A control deck that rarely attacks, and discarding mills no one.

Gix, Yawgmoth Praetor.text: **Thranduil:** Combat draws off the Elf tokens and menace bodies, and "{4}{B}{B}{B}, Discard X cards" turns the Elf mana into free casts while binning Elves for Thranduil. **Glarb:** Few attackers for the draw half; the exile-and-cast sink is strong but needs BBB and a hand to discard.

Isareth the Awakener.text: **Thranduil:** Reanimates on attack for {X}; spend it on non-Elf ETB targets (Cloud of Darkness, Silumgar, Sheoldred, Overlord) that Yarok doubles, so Thranduil keeps his Elf tools; a returned creature is exiled if it leaves. **Glarb:** Own-yard reanimation is not the plan.

Kaervek, the Punisher.text: "exile up to one target black card from your graveyard and copy it. You may cast the copy." **Thranduil:** Maralen, Yawgmoth and removal commit crimes; copy Infernal Grasp, Price of Fame or Vile Offering — not Deathbloom, Izoni or Trystan, whose abilities Thranduil borrows. **Glarb:** The Tutelages commit a crime every turn, and the yard holds black removal, Damnation and Breach the Multiverse to recast.

Tatsunari, Toad Rider.text: **Thranduil:** About six enchantments to trigger Keimi. **Glarb:** About eight (Corrosion, the Tutelages, Rhystic Study…), so Keimi drains a little; still a weak body.

Yahenni, Undying Partisan.text: "Sacrifice another creature" for free. **Thranduil:** Can turn an Elf on the board into a yard tool, but Yawgmoth's outlet also draws. **Glarb:** About 20 creatures and nothing to gain from a sacrifice.

Davriel, Soul Broker.text: **Thranduil:** −3 "perpetually gets −3/−3" is real removal and +1 punishes attacks, but −3 leaves it on 1 loyalty and the list already counts 15 interaction. **Glarb:** Same card here; the discard adds nothing to mill and interaction is already 16.

Doctor Doom, Unrivaled.text: **Thranduil:** "{T}: You draw a card" is repeatable card advantage on a 4-mana lifelink body; it triggers Elrond, Moon-Reader and Ioreth untaps it for a second draw. Not in the list. **Glarb:** In the list: every tap is a draw the Tutelages and Psychic Corrosion turn into mill, and once our library is empty it wins outright.

Erebos, God of the Dead.text: "{1}{B}, Pay 2 life: Draw a card." **Thranduil:** A repeatable mana sink for the Elf mana engines that turns spare mana into cards. **Glarb:** Same, and each draw mills two through Psychic Corrosion or a Tutelage; Sheoldred's lifegain pays the life.

Gisa, Glorious Resurrector.text: **Thranduil:** Touches nothing in our yard and only fires after removal; the decayed bodies feed Yawgmoth and Izoni, but that is a board-state payoff. **Glarb:** Damnation and spot removal give it bodies, but it EXILES their dying creatures, which Drown in the Loch, Consuming Aberration and Sheoldred's chapter III want in their graveyard.

Kels, Fight Fixer.text: **Thranduil:** "Whenever you sacrifice a creature, you may pay {U/B}… draw" stacks with Yawgmoth and Izoni, now in the list, and a sacrificed Elf lands in Thranduil's yard; a second payoff, not an engine alone. **Glarb:** Few creatures to sacrifice; off-plan.

Liliana of the Dark Realms.text: **Thranduil:** +1 fetches any Swamp card, including the typed duals and triome (10 Swamps in the list), so it fixes and feeds Sindarin Liege's landfall each turn; −3 is about −4/−4. **Glarb:** Also 10 Swamps, but a land a turn is not a draw, so nothing is milled.

Kingpin, Wilson Fisk.text: **Thranduil:** Two Treasures once a turn whenever you sacrifice a creature; Yawgmoth and Izoni are outlets, but the Elves already make the mana. **Glarb:** Almost no sacrifice outlets; a 4-mana menace body.

Lo and Li, Royal Advisors.text: **Thranduil:** Self-target mill four is repeatable fuel (Kagha casts from it that turn), but three mana an activation. **Glarb:** "{2}{U/B}: Target player mills four" at instant speed grows huge with Bruvac and The Water Crystal; it and the other Advisors (Bruvac, The Master of Lake-town) grow when they mill.

Lord Dregg, Insect Invader.text: **Thranduil:** Yawgmoth's sacrifices turn on the Insect tokens, and {3}{G} sacrificing a token draws a card; generic. **Glarb:** Few permanents leave our battlefield.

Madame Hydra, Reanimated.text: **Thranduil:** Repeatable self-mill 2 on entry and each attack (Yarok doubles the entry, Sidisi makes Zombies off milled creatures) on a body that grows with a 45-creature deck's yard. **Glarb:** Mills your own library and counts your own creature cards; off-plan.

Massacre Girl, Known Killer.text: **Thranduil:** Draws when an opposing creature dies with toughness below 1, and the list does that: High Perfect Morcant's blight per Elf entering, Yawgmoth's -1/-1 counters, Gloom Ripper's -0/-X, Garruk's +2. **Glarb:** Few attackers and one -X/-X effect (Theorix Charm); a 4/4 menace.

Moonstone, Harsh Mistress.text: "Whenever you discard a card, you may exile that card … you may play that card." **Thranduil:** The exile is a "may": keep Elf discards for Thranduil, replay non-Elf ones; Thranduil's loot, Fauna Shaman and Yawgmoth's discard turn card-positive, and the exile triggers Teval and Oasis. **Glarb:** Few discards: two Tutelage loots and the end-step trim Reed Richards removes.

One Ring to Rule Them All.text: **Thranduil:** Chapter II "Destroy all nonlegendary creatures" kills 18 of the list's creatures, most of the mana Elves. **Glarb:** II is nearly one-sided (6 nonlegendary creatures), I mills each player by your Ring-bearer's power, and III drains for each creature card in THEIR graveyard, which the mill fills. Strong add.

Rev, Tithe Extractor.text: **Thranduil:** Treasure and a stolen card per connecting combat; Elf tokens and Lathril's menace attack. **Glarb:** The same trigger needs combat damage, and the list rarely attacks.

Sarevok the Usurper.text: **Thranduil:** +X/+0 from creature cards in our yard is a real number here, but pumping one attacker is not the plan. **Glarb:** Few creature cards in its own yard; a weak scaler.

Yawgmoth, Thran Physician.text: **Thranduil:** In the list. A free repeatable sac-draw (fodder from Imperious Perfect, Sidisi, Sindarin Liege, Morcant's Eyes, Izoni) bins nontoken Elves for Thranduil, and the discard-proliferate bins cards and ticks seven walkers. **Glarb:** Little fodder (a few walker tokens); proliferate helps nine walkers.

Whisper, Blood Liturgist.text: "{T}, Sacrifice two creatures: Return target creature card from your graveyard to the battlefield." **Thranduil:** Elf, Zombie and Plant tokens pay the cost; reanimate a non-Elf bomb (Sheoldred, Muldrotha) and trigger Kotis, Teval and Roots. **Glarb:** Few tokens, and own-yard recursion is not the plan.

Aclazotz, Deepest Betrayal // Temple of.text: **Thranduil:** A strong 5-mana flier with hand attack, but it feeds no graveyard, makes no mana and draws only off an empty hand, in a crowded 5-drop slot; engine cards come first. **Glarb:** Castable off the top (MV 5) and returns as a land when it dies, but discard is not mill and nothing here pays it off.

Ashiok, Wicked Manipulator.text: **Thranduil:** +1 is card selection and −2 makes two bodies, but nothing here touches the graveyard engine; a generic 5-mana walker. **Glarb:** The pay-life static only meets the three shocklands and Jace's compleated cost (Phyrexian Arena and Infernal Grasp LOSE life, not pay it). +1 puts a card in hand without a draw trigger, and −7 counts only YOUR exiled cards — weaker than the three Ashioks already in.

Black Widow, Daring Operative.text: **Thranduil:** The ETB mill 3 is real fuel and Yarok doubles it, but the drain (creature cards in your yard) is combat-gated on a 5-drop, and Dawnhand Eulogist already mills 3 for 4. **Glarb:** Mills your own library and counts your own creature cards; Glarb's mill fills the opponent's yard, so it is off-plan.

Drana, the Last Bloodchief.text: "defending player chooses a nonlegendary creature card in your graveyard." **Thranduil:** Recursion every attack that also triggers Teval, Oasis, Insidious Roots and Kotis, but the opponent picks the worst of ~18 nonlegendary creatures — usually a mana Elf whose ability Thranduil was using (G-42). **Glarb:** Own-yard recursion with almost no creature cards there; off-plan.

Garruk, Veiled Butcher.text: In Thranduil's list. **Thranduil:** Interaction (+2 −4/−1, −2 edict paid with a token) plus −3 card advantage; exiling their dying creatures costs nothing here. **Glarb:** "If a creature an opponent controls would die, exile it instead" keeps cards out of the yard Consuming Aberration, Drown in the Loch, Breach and Ashiok's −5 read (G-42), so it is a weaker fit than its removal suggests.

Ghoulcaller Gisa.text: **Thranduil:** Sacrificing a nontoken Elf moves its ability into Thranduil's yard, and the tap triggers Elrond, Moon-Reader; Elves are small, so X is 1–2 Zombies. Yawgmoth does the sac-outlet job better, with a card drawn. **Glarb:** Few creatures to sacrifice and no mill tie.

Gisa, the Hellraiser.text: "Whenever you commit a crime, create two tapped 2/2 … Zombie Rogue" tokens (once a turn). **Thranduil:** Maralen's opponent-targeting ETB, Yawgmoth's counters, Deathrite and the removal commit crimes; the Zombies fuel Yawgmoth, Izoni and Insidious Roots, and Gisa pumps Kotis and Teval/Sidisi Zombies. **Glarb:** Teferi's and Sphinx's Tutelage target an opponent on every draw, so two blockers a turn; defence, not the mill plan.

Junji, the Midnight Sky.text: **Thranduil:** Its death trigger reanimates a non-Dragon (prefer a non-Elf or the opponent's, to keep Thranduil's tools); sac outlets (Yawgmoth, Izoni, Vraska +2) fire it on demand, and Kotis or Muldrotha can recast it. **Glarb:** A 5-mana flier castable off the top; its reanimation can take a creature from their milled yard, but few sac outlets.

Lo and Li, Twin Tutors.text: "Search your library for a Lesson or Noble card." **Thranduil:** Five Noble targets (Lathril, High Perfect Morcant, Elrond, Maralen, Thranduil, Sindarin Liege) at 5 mana, and Nobles gain lifelink. **Glarb:** One target (Princess Yue) and no Lessons.

Maha, Its Feathers Night.text: **Thranduil:** "Creatures your opponents control have base toughness 1" turns High Perfect Morcant's blight on every Elf entry, Yawgmoth's −1/−1 counter and Gloom Ripper into removal; ward—discard feeds the yard. **Glarb:** A 5-mana flier off the top; the static has few partners here.

Sauron, the Necromancer.text: **Thranduil:** Each attack exiles a creature card from your yard for a one-turn copy whose ETB fires (Gloom Ripper, Cloud of Darkness, Sheoldred's edict); aim it at non-Elf cards (G-42), and it still trims the reanimation targets. **Glarb:** Its own yard holds few creatures; the mill fills theirs.

Seizan, Perverter of Truth.text: **Thranduil:** Symmetric draw two each upkeep; with Leovold in the list the opponent draws only one — a two-card combo. **Glarb:** "That player loses 2 life and draws two cards": the opponent loses two library cards a turn (and 4 life to Sheoldred, the Apocalypse), and your two draws mill four through Corrosion. Symmetric, which this deck wants (Dictate of Kruphix).

Seymour Flux.text: **Thranduil:** A draw per upkeep on a body; card advantage but no graveyard tie. **Glarb:** A Phyrexian Arena on a body (Arena is in); every draw mills, and Glarb casts it off the top.

Shredder, Shadow Master.text: **Thranduil:** A 5-mana combat finisher (half their life) with no synergy. **Glarb:** Same; a beater is not the plan.

Skithiryx, the Blight Dragon.text: **Thranduil:** A lone infect threat. **Glarb:** Same; no poison plan.

Syr Konrad, the Grim.text: **Thranduil:** Pings on every creature milled, dying or leaving the yard, and {1}{B} self-mills; 1-point pings for 5 mana. **Glarb:** "A creature card is put into a graveyard from anywhere" counts their milled creatures, so big mills deal real damage.

Tergrid, God of Fright // Tergrid's Lant.text: **Thranduil:** Sheoldred, Whispering One's upkeep edict and Garruk's −2 and −3 hand it a permanent each time. **Glarb:** M.O.D.O.K.'s edict on our second draw each turn and Sheoldred's ETB and chapter II (discard three) do the same; Glarb casts it off the top. The Lantern face forces it alone.

Witch-king of Angmar.text: "Discard a card: Witch-king … gains indestructible." **Thranduil:** A free instant-speed discard outlet to bin an Elf for Thranduil (or feed Moonstone), but card-negative on a 5-mana body. **Glarb:** A defensive edict against attackers; the Ring tempt does nothing.

Doctor Doom.text: **Thranduil:** Two 3/3 Doombots (doubled by Yarok) feed Yawgmoth, Izoni and Insidious Roots, plus an end-step draw for 6 mana. **Glarb:** Not the list's Doctor Doom, Unrivaled; this one's end-step draw is a mill trigger each turn and it casts off the top as MV 6.

Bolas's Citadel.text: **Thranduil:** Playing lands and spells off the top for life is raw card advantage, and the cheap Elves cost 1–2 life; `{B}{B}{B}` is fine on 20 black sources, but it bins nothing. **Glarb:** Glarb already plays lands and MV 4+ off the top; Citadel adds the cheap spells and pays life instead of mana for the big ones. Cards played off the top are not draws, so no Tutelage mill. 20 B sources.

Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni.text: **Thranduil:** Reanimates THEIR creature on combat damage; Ninjutsu has few unblocked attackers to return. **Glarb:** Their yard is full, but the list rarely attacks, so the trigger seldom happens.

Lich's Mastery.text: **Thranduil:** Every life paid (Yawgmoth, shocklands) exiles a card, which eats Thranduil's yard. **Glarb:** With Sheoldred, the Apocalypse each draw gains 2 and draws 2 more until our library is empty, milling them via the Tutelages; Doctor Doom's tap then wins. Losing Mastery loses the game.

Tetzimoc, Primal Death.text: **Thranduil:** A one-sided sweeper only after paying {B} per prey counter from hand on earlier turns; slow. **Glarb:** Same, and casting it off the top skips the prey setup.

The Cloning of Shredder.text: "Exile target creature card from your graveyard. Create a token that's a copy" — three nonlegendary copies. **Thranduil:** On a non-Elf: three Sheoldred edicts, Cloud of Darkness kills or Silumgar steals, doubled by Yarok. **Glarb:** Works only if a creature reached your yard (Sphinx Mindbreaker binned by surveil = 30 mill).

Vraska, Betrayal's Sting.text: In Thranduil's list. **Thranduil:** 0: draw and proliferate (walkers, Marwyn/Dionus/Kotis counters); −2 removal; a 6-drop. **Glarb:** The 0 draw mills through Corrosion and both Tutelages and proliferates nine walkers; −2 neutralises a creature, and Glarb can cast it off the top.

K'rrik, Son of Yawgmoth.text: **Thranduil:** Life for black mana in a green-mana deck whose Elves already make plenty. **Glarb:** Few black spells to grow it; no payoff for the life.

Count Nefaria.text: **Thranduil:** A 7-mana flier, {3} cheaper after a sacrifice (Yawgmoth makes that easy), but no graveyard, mana or card text. **Glarb:** A vanilla flier with no draw, mill or interaction.

Morlun, Devourer of Spiders.text: **Thranduil:** An X sink for the Elf mana engines: X damage to the opponent plus an X/X lifelinker, but no graveyard tie. **Glarb:** Far less mana to pour in, and a beater does nothing for the mill.

Celeborn the Wise.text: **Thranduil:** A legendary Elf entering is a Thranduil loot (twice with Yarok in the list), but it has no activated ability for the yard and its scry/pump is combat-only. **Glarb:** Scry 1 when Celeborn himself attacks triggers Matoya and Proft — a 4-mana combat-gated draw.

Goreclaw, Terror of Qal Sisma.text: Generic big-creature support. **Thranduil:** Ten of its 45 creatures have power 4 or more; the rest are small Elves and mana dorks. **Glarb:** Its few big creatures are cast off the top anyway, and it neither draws nor mills.

Kona, Rescue Beastie.text: **Thranduil:** Needs Kona tapped; Eladamri's tap-two cost or an attack does it, then a free permanent from hand (Sheoldred, Muldrotha). **Glarb:** No tap plan beyond attacking.

Leyline Immersion.text: **Thranduil:** Ward 2 and five spell-only mana on a legend that doesn't need its {T} (Muldrotha, Sidisi, Yarok); Ioreth and Kinnan add more. A 4-mana ramp aura beside 11 mana creatures. **Glarb:** Glarb's tap is surveil, so it goes on Matoya or Proft; ramp in a deck that casts its top end free.

Mythweaver Poq.text: **Thranduil:** Doubles one land drop a turn (any nontoken land), but the mana Elves already ramp. **Glarb:** Extra lands push toward MV 4+ casts off the top, but it is a 4-mana green body with no draw or mill.

Oyaminartok, Polar Werebear.text: An off-plan beater: hexproof until it deals damage, Food for spellbook drafts. **Thranduil:** No graveyard or mana tie. **Glarb:** Neither draws nor mills, and GG on the splash colour.

Radagast of Rhosgobel.text: **Thranduil:** 45 creatures, so the first one each turn costing {2} less is steady ramp — mana synergy on a 2/5 with no graveyard tie. **Glarb:** About 20 creatures, several cast off the top by Glarb anyway; flash on one a turn suits control, but it neither draws nor mills.

Tyvar Kell.text: **Thranduil:** "Elves you control have {T}: Add {B}" fixes black on 33 Elves (Thranduil included), 0 makes an Elf a turn, +1 untaps a mana Elf, and the −6 emblem draws two per Elf spell; real mana synergy, but its value scales with Elf count and costs {G}{G}. **Glarb:** One Elf in the list; off-plan.

Ashaya, Soul of the Wild.text: "Nontoken creatures you control are Forest lands." **Thranduil:** Each creature entering becomes landfall for Thranduil, Sindarin Liege (an Elf token) and grows Wrenn and Seven's Treefolk, but it switches off Kinnan, whose trigger needs a nonland permanent. **Glarb:** Only Ruin Crab cares; a GG body in a list whose green is a splash.

Bosco, Just a Bear.text: "create a Food token for each legendary creature you control." **Thranduil:** Many Foods off the legend-heavy board, but nothing in the list uses Food. **Glarb:** Same, on a green splash.

Greensleeves, Maro-Sorcerer.text: **Thranduil:** A 3/3 Badger per land; Wrenn and Seven's 0, Teval and Kamahl's Druidic Vow put extra lands in, and the tokens feed Yawgmoth, but nothing ties it to the graveyard engine. **Glarb:** One land a turn plus Growth Spiral; a 5-mana threat with no draw or mill.

Wrenn and Seven.text: **Thranduil:** In the list. +1 bins nonlands and hands you lands every turn, 0 is a land burst for landfall, −3 is a huge body and −8 rebuys the yard: graveyard, mana and card advantage on one card. **Glarb:** Its self-mill is not the plan; the Treefolk is a big blocker with 36 lands.

Garruk, Caller of Beasts.text: "+1: Reveal the top five … all creature cards … into your hand." **Thranduil:** 45 creatures in 100 cards: about two cards a turn, and each legendary Elf found is a Thranduil loot when cast. Card advantage comes first. **Glarb:** 20 creatures, so +1 finds one, the reveal is not a draw (no mill), and {G}{G} sits on a splash.

Mitotic Ultimus.text: A 9-mana trampler discounted by your biggest creature. **Thranduil:** No graveyard tie, and its biggest bodies are 6-power. **Glarb:** Nothing to do with drawing or milling.

Invasion of Ikoria // Zilortha, Apex of.text: "search your library and/or graveyard for a non-Human creature card with mana value X or less and put it onto the battlefield." **Thranduil:** A flexible tutor or reanimation (Priest of Titania at X=2, Muldrotha at 6); only Kinnan, Ioreth and Yawgmoth are Human. Competes with Kamahl's Druidic Vow and Journey. **Glarb:** {X}{G}{G} on a green splash for few targets (Sheoldred, the Apocalypse at 6 mana).

Golbez, Crystal Collector.text: **Thranduil:** Needs artifacts and the list runs none. **Glarb:** Five rocks and the Water Crystal give a surveil (a Matoya draw) now and then; four artifacts for the recursion is rare.

Lazav, the Multifarious.text: "{X}: Lazav becomes a copy of target creature card in your graveyard with mana value X" — no exile, so no G-42 cost. **Thranduil:** Copying an Elf duplicates what Thranduil already borrows, but a binned Muldrotha, Teval, Kotis or Sidisi becomes a second copy for X. Not in the list. **Glarb:** Surveil 1 triggers Matoya and Proft; few creature cards to copy.

Krydle of Baldur's Gate.text: **Thranduil:** A 2-mana legendary Elf is a cheap Thranduil loot, and the {2} unblockable grant lets Lathril connect; its own mill 1 / scry 1 is negligible. **Glarb:** The scry triggers Matoya and the mill is doubled, but only after combat damage from a 2/2.

The Ancient One.text: "{2}{U}{B}: Draw a card, then discard a card … target player mills cards equal to its mana value." **Thranduil:** A repeatable loot that can mill you (yard fuel), triggers Elrond, and becomes an 8/8 for 2 once descend 8 is met. Not in the list. **Glarb:** Each loot is a draw that mills, plus the discard's MV; descend is slow here.

Zimone the Calculating // Simple Subtrac.text: **Thranduil:** Prepared whenever cards go from library to graveyard (every mill and surveil), so it can cast a {1}{U} perpetual −3/−0 most turns; defensive, not removal. **Glarb:** Glarb's surveil prepares it each turn too; same small effect.

Lazav, Familiar Stranger.text: **Thranduil:** Crimes are rare (spot removal), and its "may exile a card from a graveyard" is optional, so no G-42 cost, but little gain. **Glarb:** Teferi's and Sphinx's Tutelage target an opponent on every draw, so it grows each turn; copying a milled creature exiles cards Drown in the Loch and Aberration count.

Locke Cole.text: **Thranduil:** A combat-gated loot on a 3-mana body; the list has better yard fillers. **Glarb:** Deathtouch lifelink blocker whose loot draws a milling card on damage, but it must connect.

Ringsight.text: **Thranduil:** Thranduil is BGU, so it finds any coloured card — Priest of Titania or a missing engine piece; Fauna Shaman already tutors creatures. **Glarb:** Glarb is BGU too: a 3-mana tutor for Psychic Corrosion or Bruvac in a singleton deck.

Rona, Disciple of Gix.text: "{4}, {T}: Exile the top card of your library" (cast it later). **Thranduil:** A mana sink for the Elf mana that Ioreth untaps; its ETB yard exile should take a non-Elf legend (triggers Teval). **Glarb:** Reaches the MV-under-4 cards Glarb cannot cast off the top, but exiling is not drawing, so no mill.

Emet-Selch of the Third Seat.text: **Thranduil:** "Spells you cast from your graveyard cost {2} less" discounts Muldrotha, Kotis and Kagha recasts, but the recast half wants instants and sorceries and the list runs seven. **Glarb:** 21 instants and sorceries to recast, but it needs an opponent to lose life, and Sheoldred, the Apocalypse is nearly the only source.

Xande, Dark Mage.text: A beater that grows with noncreature, nonland cards in your yard. **Thranduil:** Self-mill puts some there, but it adds nothing to the engine. **Glarb:** Spent spells grow it, but a beater is not how Glarb wins.

Phenax, God of Deception.text: **Thranduil:** Can target yourself to mill X for fuel, but the Elves are 1–2 toughness and tap for mana. **Glarb:** On the bench. 12 of 20 creatures have toughness 4+ (Glarb, Bruvac, Matoya, Reed, both Sheoldreds, Silumgar, M.O.D.O.K.), each a mill engine Bruvac doubles. Indestructible.

Uchbenbak, the Great Mistake.text: **Thranduil:** A self-recurring beater ranks behind engines; its one tie is the descend return, which triggers Teval, Insidious Roots and Kotis. **Glarb:** A beater.

Ultimecia, Time Sorceress.text: **Thranduil:** Surveil 2 on enter/attack bins Elves; the extra turn's "exile eight cards from your graveyard" is optional, and a self-milled yard has eight non-Elf cards to spend (G-42), but it costs eight mana. **Glarb:** Each surveil draws off Matoya and Proft; its own yard is free to exile, and the extra turn is an extra draw step.

Ashiok, Sculptor of Fears.text: In Glarb's list. **Thranduil:** +2 draws and mills each player two, so your two feed the yard every turn, and −5 reanimates from either graveyard; a real add, but a 6-drop competing with Vraska and Liliana. **Glarb:** +2's draw triggers Corrosion and both Tutelages on top of its own mill two, and −5 steals a creature from the yard the deck fills.

Tezzeret, Master of the Bridge.text: **Thranduil:** No artifacts. **Glarb:** Six artifacts (four mana rocks, The Water Crystal, M.O.D.O.K.), so +2 drains two or three; an artifact-deck walker.

Krang & Shredder.text: "each opponent exiles cards from the top of their library until they exile a nonland card" on enter and attack; Disappear casts one free. **Thranduil:** Sac outlets meet Disappear, but it is a 6-drop with no yard synergy. **Glarb:** Library exile with a 6/7 body Glarb can cast from the top, but only Mind Stone, Kaito's ninjutsu and Princess Yue reliably make a permanent leave.

Xanathar, Guild Kingpin.text: "that player can't cast spells" this turn, and you may play their top card. **Thranduil:** A 6-mana value engine with no yard synergy. **Glarb:** Shuts off their responses on your turn and plays their top card, castable from the top by Glarb; strong, but the theft is not a draw.

Prototype X-8.text: "Whenever another creature you control enters, if you cast it, sacrifice it. Conjure a duplicate." **Thranduil:** Every cast Elf triggers its ETB twice (two loots for a legend), and the original lands in the yard where Thranduil borrows its ability; costs {2} less per creature card in the self-milled yard. Not in the list. **Glarb:** Few creature cards in its yard, so near 10 mana.

Chevill, Bane of Monsters.text: **Thranduil:** The bounty draw fires when the marked creature dies, and the list's dozen-plus removal makes that happen, but it is a 2-drop with no graveyard tie. **Glarb:** Same; the removal suite cashes bounties, yet it neither draws repeatably nor mills.

Dina, Soul Steeper.text: "Whenever you gain life, each opponent loses 1 life." **Thranduil:** Lifegain is incidental (Trystan, Deathrite, Dawnhand, Izoni) and the sac outlet gives no card. **Glarb:** Sheoldred's draw lifegain triggers it, but drain is not the win.

Slimefoot, Thallid Transplant.text: "Whenever a Swamp or Forest enters under your control, draft a card" from its spellbook. **Thranduil:** 20 of 36 lands are Swamps or Forests, and Teval, Wrenn and Seven and the Sindarin Liege adventure add land drops, so it is a card most turns. **Glarb:** 14 qualify, and drafting is not a draw, so it mills no one.

Vraska Joins Up.text: "Whenever a legendary creature you control deals combat damage to a player, draw a card." **Thranduil:** 27 legendary creatures with fliers and menace (Teval, Maralen, Lathril, Silumgar), and deathtouch for every blocker. **Glarb:** A control deck that rarely attacks; Glarb already has deathtouch.

Dina, Essence Brewer.text: **Thranduil:** "Whenever you sacrifice a creature, draw a card" (once a turn) pairs with Yawgmoth and Izoni, now in the list, and with its own outlet; tokens are fodder and a sacrificed Elf lands in Thranduil's yard. **Glarb:** No sacrifice fodder or outlets; off-plan.

Long Feng, Grand Secretariat.text: **Thranduil:** Sacrifices (Yawgmoth, Izoni, Vraska +2) and dying creatures put +1/+1 counters, which Yawgmoth and Morcant proliferate — minor. **Glarb:** Few deaths or counters.

Pharika, God of Affliction.text: **Thranduil:** `{B}{G}`: exile a creature card from a graveyard, its owner gets a 1/1 deathtouch Snake — on your own non-Elf cards that is a Snake plus Teval's Zombie and an Insidious Roots Plant; never point it at an Elf (G-42). **Glarb:** Shrinks the opponent's yard that Drown and Consuming Aberration count, and hands them deathtouch tokens.

Sarulf, Realm Eater.text: "exile each other nonland permanent with mana value less than or equal to" its counters — yours too. **Thranduil:** Would exile your own cheap mana Elves and enchantments. **Glarb:** Can be held at one or two counters, but the MV 3 engines (Psychic Corrosion, the Tutelages) die with a bigger wipe.

Sméagol, Helpful Guide.text: Its Ring trigger needs a creature of yours to die that turn. **Thranduil:** Yawgmoth and Izoni sacrifice a token on demand, and the stolen land is ramp plus Sindarin Liege landfall, but the opponent mill does nothing here. **Glarb:** The mill-until-land is on-plan, but nothing sacrifices its few creatures.

The Mycotyrant.text: **Thranduil:** Power counts only Fungi (itself plus its tokens), but each permanent card the self-mill bins is a descend, so a mill turn makes 2–3 Fungus tokens: Yawgmoth/Izoni fodder and mana with Insidious Roots. **Glarb:** Its own permanents rarely hit the yard (Glarb's surveil only).

Furgul, Quag Nurturer.text: **Thranduil:** A legendary Elf (Thranduil loot) whose `{T}, Sacrifice a creature: Add {G}` equal to power is worth borrowing from the yard, and it conjures a Leech body each turn; Yawgmoth already fills the sac slot. Alchemy (conjure). **Glarb:** A creature sac outlet does nothing for draw-to-mill.

Nissa of Shadowed Boughs.text: **Thranduil:** −5 puts a creature with MV ≤ lands from hand or yard onto the battlefield; Wrenn and Seven's 0, Kamahl's Vow, Teval, Kagha and Muldrotha add land drops, so loyalty climbs. **Glarb:** Own-yard reanimation is not the plan.

Nemata, Primeval Warden.text: **Thranduil:** Saprolings feed Yawgmoth and Insidious Roots, but it is a slow draw engine. **Glarb:** "If a creature an opponent controls would die, exile it instead" keeps cards out of the yard Consuming Aberration, Drown in the Loch and the reanimation spells read (G-42); the Saproling draw is slow.

Tyvar the Bellicose.text: **Thranduil:** A legendary Elf (Thranduil loot) that grows each mana creature by the mana it makes (big on Priest of Titania) and gives attacking Elves deathtouch; no activated ability, so nothing to borrow. **Glarb:** Two mana creatures; off-plan.

Vraska, Golgari Queen.text: In Thranduil's list: +2 sacrifices a token or spent permanent to draw, −3 kills MV 3 or less. **Why not Glarb's:** +2 needs fodder the list barely has; −3 is fine removal.

Ygra, Eater of All.text: "Other creatures are Food artifacts" with a {2}, sacrifice ability. **Thranduil:** Every creature becomes its own sac outlet (binning Elves), but it turns off Go for the Throat against their creatures. **Glarb:** A 6/6 body; same Go for the Throat conflict.

Yargle and Multani.text: **Thranduil:** A big vanilla body that Sheoldred, Whispering One or Atzal could reanimate, but with no evasion. **Glarb:** A vanilla body; nothing here wants it.

Beledros Witherbloom.text: **Thranduil:** A Pest every upkeep feeds Yawgmoth and Izoni (sacrifice: draw), Insidious Roots mana and Eladamri's tap cost, but it is a 7-drop with no graveyard tie. **Glarb:** Glarb can cast it off the top, but it neither draws nor mills.

Witherbloom, the Balancer.text: **Thranduil:** Affinity for creatures makes it cheap in a 45-creature deck, a flying deathtouch body, but only 7 instants/sorceries get the discount. **Glarb:** 20 creatures, so it stays expensive; the discount helps 21 spells but needs bodies on board.

Arwen Undómiel.text: **Thranduil:** A 2-mana legendary Elf, so its entry is a Thranduil loot, but the counter trigger needs scry and the list scries nowhere else; its {4}{G}{U} scry 2 is a weak tool to borrow from the yard. **Glarb:** "Whenever you scry" misses Glarb's surveil; only Princess Yue and its own 6-mana scry trigger it (and Matoya).

Kinnan, Bonder Prodigy.text: **Thranduil:** In the list: "Whenever you tap a nonland permanent for mana, add one mana" adds a mana to each of the 11 mana creatures, Insidious Roots tokens and Thranduil's borrowed mana abilities, and `{5}{G}{U}` puts a non-Human creature (any Elf) from the top five onto the battlefield. **Glarb:** Boosts four rocks and two dorks; many of its creatures are Humans.

Absorbing Man.text: "Becomes a copy of up to one target artifact, non-Aura enchantment, or land" each turn. **Thranduil:** At best a second Insidious Roots or Oasis of Renewal on a fragile 4/4; it feeds nothing itself. **Glarb:** A second Psychic Corrosion, Tutelage, Water Crystal or Teferi's Ageless Insight every turn for 3 mana; it needs one on board and dies as a creature.

Albiorix, Goose Tyrant // Wild Goose Cha.text: **Thranduil:** "Draw two cards, then discard two cards" for 2 bins two cards (Elves become Thranduil's tools, anything else feeds Kotis/Muldrotha), then a 3-mana flier that grows off token sacrifices (Yawgmoth, Izoni, Vraska). **Glarb:** Two draws trigger Psychic Corrosion and both Tutelages, but discarding two is a real cost in a control deck; card-neutral.

Galadriel of Lothlórien.text: **Thranduil:** A legendary Elf for Thranduil's loot, but no Ring and no scry in the list, so its land ramp never fires. **Glarb:** "Whenever you scry" — Glarb's tap is SURVEIL, not scry; only Princess Yue scries, and nothing tempts with the Ring.

Kiora of Salt and Sand.text: **Thranduil:** Seven planeswalkers, but none reaches the −8 and the attack clause needs creatures to attack. **Glarb:** Teferi, Temporal Pilgrim gains loyalty per draw, so an 8/8 hexproof is reachable; otherwise little.

Kasmina, Enigma Sage.text: **Thranduil:** Shares +2 scry 1 with seven walkers, but scry has no payoff here. **Glarb:** Every other walker (nine of them) gains "+2: Scry 1", which Matoya and Proft turn into draws that mill; cute, low impact.

Nissa, Steward of Elements.text: **Thranduil:** The 0 drops a land or a cheap Elf off the top. **Glarb:** +2 scry 2 is a Matoya draw, and the 0 puts lands from the top into play; MV 2 from the top, so Glarb cannot cast it there.

Drowned Secrets.text: "Whenever you cast a blue spell, target player mills two cards." **Thranduil:** Self-mill on 14 blue spells is too little. **Glarb:** 42 of the 64 nonland cards are blue: a 2-mana engine that mills two (four with Bruvac) without needing a draw.

Navigator's Ruin.text: "Raid — … if you attacked this turn, target opponent mills four." **Thranduil:** Opponent-only mill; off-plan. **Glarb:** Needs an attack each turn; only Restless Reef, Kaito and Ashiok's tokens swing.

Fleet Swallower.text: "Whenever this creature attacks, target player mills half their library." **Thranduil:** A 7-mana body whose self-target attack decks you on the second swing. **Glarb:** On the bench; castable off the top and lethal with Bruvac, but no evasion or haste, where Traumatize and kicked Maddening Cacophony do it from hand.

Ashiok, Dream Render.text: **Thranduil:** −1 can mill you four a turn for fuel, and "exile each opponent's graveyard" leaves Thranduil's yard alone. **Glarb:** Cut at draft: that exile empties the yard Consuming Aberration, Drown in the Loch and Sheoldred's transform count (G-42).

Cut Your Losses.text: **Thranduil:** Self-target mills half your library as fuel (as Traumatize would), but 6 mana that does nothing on its own. **Glarb:** On the bench, screened KEY. Half a library for 6, all of it with casualty or Bruvac, and MV 6 casts off the top; Traumatize, Maddening Cacophony and Jidoor's Overture already do the job.

Altar of Dementia.text: "Sacrifice a creature: Target player mills cards equal to the sacrificed creature's power." **Thranduil:** A free instant-speed sac outlet that bins an Elf card for Thranduil on demand and can self-mill (Sidisi turns milled creatures into Zombies). **Glarb:** Fodder is thin (Theorist Illusions, Ashiok Nightmares, Teferi's Spirit); a finisher only by sacrificing Consuming Aberration.

Grindstone.text: **Thranduil:** Opponent mill is off-plan. **Glarb:** `{3}, {T}`: mill two, repeating while the two share a colour — about 2–4 a turn (doubled by Bruvac), but 3 mana every turn in a deck that wants mana open.

Villainous Wealth.text: **Thranduil:** A huge mana sink for the Elf mana engines, but not a graveyard card. **Glarb:** Exiles X of their library and casts them — real library exile, but `{X}{B}{G}{U}` competes with Tasha's Hideous Laughter, which exiles to 20 total mana value for 3.

Mind's Dilation.text: **Thranduil:** Exiles their library; no use here. **Glarb:** 7 mana; exiles one card per opponent's turn — slow as library exile.

Visions of Beyond.text: **Thranduil:** Self-mill often puts our own yard past twenty, so it turns into a 1-mana draw three late. **Glarb:** "If a graveyard has twenty or more cards in it, draw three" — the opponent's graveyard passes 20 early, so it is a 1-mana draw-three (six milled through Corrosion).

Folio of Fancies.text: **Thranduil:** Symmetric draw with no graveyard or Elf tie. **Glarb:** `{X}{X}, {T}`: each player draws X (yours trigger Corrosion and the Tutelages; theirs shrink their library and Sheoldred punishes them), or `{2}{U}, {T}`: mill them equal to hand size. Both need the tap, so one per turn; a real engine, on the bench.

Lord of the Forsaken.text: **Thranduil:** "{B}, Sacrifice another creature: Target player mills three" — a free sac outlet that targets US to stock Thranduil's yard, and its colourless mana pays for Muldrotha's and Kotis's graveyard casts. **Glarb:** The deck lacks fodder (21 creatures, few tokens); 6 mana.

Persistent Petitioners.group: Mill outlet whose cost the deck lacks
Persistent Petitioners.text: **Thranduil:** Off-plan. **Glarb:** One copy mills one a turn (more with Bruvac and the Water Crystal); the 12-card mill needs four Advisors and the list holds two others (Bruvac, Master of Lake-town), so it only works as a many-copy package.

Cruel Somnophage // Can't Wake Up.text: **Thranduil:** Can't Wake Up can target yourself (mill four for 2), then a {1}{B} body sized by creature cards in ALL graveyards — big in this creature-heavy self-mill list. **Glarb:** Mill four (doubled by Bruvac, +4 with the Water Crystal) then a scaling body; fine, but Glimpse the Unthinkable mills ten for the same 2 mana.

Gyruda, Doom of Depths.text: **Thranduil:** "Each player mills four" fuels the yard, then takes an even-MV creature from either yard — a 6-mana body plus reanimation. **Glarb:** Mills them four (eight with Bruvac) and can take their creature, but mills us too; a one-shot.

Duskmantle, House of Shadow.text: **Thranduil:** {U}{B}, {T}: mill one a turn from a land that taps only for colourless; weak fuel at a fixing cost. **Glarb:** A repeatable mill from a land slot that The Water Crystal (+4) and Bruvac scale, but it makes only colourless in a three-colour list already carrying several taplands.

Hama, the Bloodbender.text: **Thranduil:** Mills the opponent, not us; the stolen spell is a one-off. **Glarb:** Mills three and lets you cast one of their noncreature spells by waterbending — deck 22's engine piece; a 5-mana one-shot here.

Didn't Say Please.text: "Counter target spell. Its controller mills three cards." **Thranduil:** A {1}{U}{U} counter in a green-heavy list; the mill does nothing here. **Glarb:** The same card as Thought Collapse, which is in, beside Counterspell and Drown in the Loch — the first add if you want more counters.

Bloodchief's Thirst.text: **Thranduil:** "Destroy target creature or planeswalker with mana value 2 or less", or anything kicked for 4 — sorcery-speed, interchangeable with the list's removal. **Glarb:** Same; a control deck prefers its instants, but it competes for a slot.

Keening Stone.text: **Thranduil:** 11 mana to mill a player; the deck's self-mill is already cheap and it does nothing else. **Glarb:** 6 to cast and `{5}, {T}` to mill X = their graveyard — doubled by Bruvac, but the list's big mills (Traumatize, Maddening Cacophony) do it for less.

Riverchurn Monument.text: "{1}, {T}: Any number of target players each mill two"; the Exhaust mills "cards equal to the number of cards in their graveyard." **Thranduil:** Cheap self-mill, but the list has a dozen sources. **Glarb:** Mill two a turn (more with Bruvac and the Water Crystal), and the Exhaust doubles a half-milled yard.

Terisian Mindbreaker.text: "Defending player mills half their library" on attack. **Thranduil:** Opponent-only mill; off-plan. **Glarb:** Castable off the top, and Unearth gives a hasty half-library mill (all with Bruvac); a 7-mana creature doing Fleet Swallower's job.

Scavenger's Talent.text: **Thranduil:** Yawgmoth and Izoni are outlets, level 2 self-mills two per sacrifice, and level 3 trades three tokens for a reanimation; slow, mana-hungry. **Glarb:** Few creatures and no outlets; nothing here sacrifices.

Brain Freeze.text: **Thranduil:** Self-target mills three at instant speed — fuel, but a card for nothing back, where the self-mill creatures leave a body. **Glarb:** The list casts one or two spells a turn, so it is usually mill three; Bruvac and The Water Crystal scale it, still far below the big mills.

Jin-Gitaxias // The Great Synthesis.text: "Whenever you cast a noncreature spell with mana value 3 or greater, draw a card." **Thranduil:** About 14 such spells; a 5-mana draw body, not graveyard synergy. **Glarb:** About 27 such spells, each draw mills; with seven in hand the Saga's chapter I draws a handful into Psychic Corrosion. Lost its slot to Jin-Gitaxias, Core Augur, but the two have different names and both fit.

Howling Mine.text: **Thranduil:** Symmetric draw with no graveyard tie; it refills the opponent as much as us. **Glarb:** A 2-mana second Dictate of Kruphix: our extra draw triggers Psychic Corrosion and the Tutelages, theirs feeds Sheoldred, the Apocalypse and Notion Thief and shortens their library — though it refills their hand too.

Hullbreaker Horror.text: **Thranduil:** A 7-mana blue bounce engine with no graveyard or mana role. **Glarb:** An uncounterable flash lock castable off the top, but it adds no mill and bounce is tempo; situational top end.

Tamiyo, Inquisitive Student // Tamiyo, S.text: **Thranduil:** Flips on the third draw in a turn — Thranduil's loot gets there — but the walker's −3 regrows only instants/sorceries (7 here). **Glarb:** Flips on your third draw, routine here, and her −7 draws half your library, which milling through Corrosion and the Tutelages turns into a huge mill. Spicy, risky.

Niv-Mizzet, Visionary.text: **Thranduil:** Off colour identity: needs {R}. **Glarb:** Same — illegal in a BGU commander deck.

Chulane, Teller of Tales.text: Off colour identity for both BGU decks: Chulane needs {W}, so it is illegal in either Brawl list.

Kenrith's Transformation.text: "When this Aura enters, draw a card. Enchanted creature loses all abilities … 3/3." **Thranduil:** Two-mana answer to any creature that replaces itself. **Glarb:** Same, and the draw mills two.

Toxic Deluge.text: **Thranduil:** A sweeper that kills your own Elves and mana engine. **Glarb:** A second sweeper beside Damnation, and choosing X can spare Glarb's tougher blockers.

Murderous Rider // Swift End.text: "Destroy target creature or planeswalker. You lose 2 life." **Thranduil:** Instant kill plus a lifelink body later; interchangeable with Go for the Throat. The body goes to the library bottom, not the yard. **Glarb:** Same.

Saw It Coming.text: **Thranduil:** A {U}{U} counter in a G/B-weighted list. **Glarb:** A flexible 3-mana counter (foretell 2); competes with Counterspell and Thought Collapse.

Memory Lapse.text: **Thranduil:** A tap-out creature deck rarely holds a counter. **Glarb:** Counters but puts the spell back on top of their library — it delays and undoes one mill.

Feed the Swarm.text: **Thranduil:** Also kills an enchantment — one of the few noncreature answers beside Trystan's Command and Vraska's −3; you lose life equal to its mana value. **Glarb:** Same answer; Assassin's Trophy and Cyclonic Rift already cover noncreature permanents, so it competes on cost.

Tear Asunder.text: **Thranduil:** Kicked, it exiles any nonland permanent — only Vraska, Golgari Queen's −3 answers an artifact now. Good add. **Glarb:** Kicked, a 4-mana exile-anything; the deck has Assassin's Trophy and Cyclonic Rift already.

Anoint with Affliction.text: **Thranduil:** "Exile target creature if it has mana value 3 or less" — a cheap instant exile, but the cap misses the big threats; Heartless Act, Go for the Throat and Infernal Grasp already fill the 2-mana slot. **Glarb:** Same cap; its six spot-removal spells are unconditional or near it.

Fatal Push.text: **Thranduil:** Mana value 2 or less without revolt; Yawgmoth's sacrifices turn on the MV 4 mode. Narrow against Brawl's bigger threats. **Glarb:** Same, with fewer ways to turn on revolt.

Bitter Triumph.text: "Discard a card or pay 3 life. Destroy target creature or planeswalker." **Thranduil:** 2-mana instant kill whose discard bins an Elf for Thranduil (or a non-Elf for Moonstone). **Glarb:** Same kill; pay the 3 life rather than a card, since every card drawn is mill.

Sheoldred's Edict.text: **Thranduil:** Instant edict: a nontoken creature, a creature token or a planeswalker. Beats hexproof; interchangeable. **Glarb:** Same.

Mystic Snake.text: "Flash. When this creature enters, counter target spell." **Thranduil:** A counter on a creature that Muldrotha and Kotis can recast from the yard; {U}{U} on a G/B base. **Glarb:** A counter on a body; MV 4 casts off the top at instant speed.

Pongify.text: "Destroy target creature … Its controller creates a 3/3 green Ape." **Thranduil:** One-mana answer to any bomb, at the cost of a 3/3. **Glarb:** Same.

Talisman of Resilience.text: "{T}: Add {B} or {G}." **Thranduil:** A plain rock behind ~13 creature mana sources (Kinnan gives it a bonus, as he does every dork). **Glarb:** The B/G pair misses blue; cut at draft for Kaito, Bane of Nightmares.

Cultivate.text: **Thranduil:** Two basics, one to hand for Thranduil, Sindarin Liege's landfall; the list already runs 12 mana Elves plus Kinnan, which ramp harder. **Glarb:** Slower than the seven rocks and dorks in the list.

Nature's Lore.text: **Thranduil:** Fetches any Forest-typed land untapped — Overgrown Tomb, Breeding Pool, Zagoth Triome — and triggers Thranduil, Sindarin Liege's landfall; the list already has 12 mana Elves plus Kinnan. **Glarb:** Same fixing; 7 ramp pieces already.

Farseek.text: **Thranduil:** Finds a typed dual (Overgrown Tomb, Watery Grave, Breeding Pool, Zagoth Triome) tapped; with 11 mana creatures it is below the bar. **Glarb:** Same targets plus Sunken Hollow; a 2-mana ramp spell in a deck with fewer mana creatures.

Delighted Halfling.text: **Thranduil:** Any colour for legendary spells, uncounterable — 38 legendary nonland cards here, and Kinnan adds a mana each tap; in the yard it lends Thranduil nothing. **Glarb:** 26 legendary spells too, but green is the light colour (15 sources) and Birds and Paradise Druid already fill the 1-drop fixer slot.

Thought Scour.text: "Target player mills two cards. Draw a card." **Thranduil:** Target yourself: 1-mana instant fuel and a card. **Glarb:** Target them: mill two (four with Bruvac) and the draw mills two more; the draft cut it for Theorix Charm.

Opt.text: **Thranduil:** A cantrip with no synergy. **Glarb:** Scry 1 then draw — with Matoya that is two draws, four milled with one Tutelage. A cheap filler; Brainstorm is in.

Preordain.text: "Scry 2, then draw a card." **Thranduil:** Scry bottoms cards instead of binning them. **Glarb:** The scry triggers Matoya and Proft and the draw mills; a cheap cantrip competing with Brainstorm.

Consider.text: **Thranduil:** Surveil 1 can bin an Elf, plus a draw — a 1-mana cantrip with no other hook. **Glarb:** "Surveil 1. Draw a card": surveil triggers Matoya (and Proft), so two draws for 1 mana, each milling through Corrosion and both Tutelages.

Memory Deluge.text: **Thranduil:** Blue selection at UU; no graveyard or Elf tie. **Glarb:** Two of the top X, then flashback for two more (11 mana in all); it puts cards into hand rather than drawing, so Corrosion and the Tutelages don't trigger. Instant selection Glarb can cast off the top; on the bench.

The Everflowing Well // The Myriad Pools.text: **Thranduil:** Mill two, then draw two — the mill feeds Thranduil, and descend 8 flips it into a land that copies permanent spells. **Glarb:** Two draws mill four through Corrosion alone, more with the Tutelages. Either is fine.

Sokka's Haiku.text: "Counter target spell. Draw a card, then mill three cards." **Thranduil:** A counter that self-mills three, but 5 mana with {U}{U}. **Glarb:** A cantrip counter Glarb can cast off the top at instant speed; the mill three hits YOU.

Arcane Epiphany.text: **Thranduil:** Plain blue draw at UU in a G/B-heavy list; no graveyard or Elf tie. **Glarb:** "Draw three cards" for 4 (Glarb is a Wizard), castable off the top at MV 5; each draw mills through Corrosion and both Tutelages. Fine, but the repeatable engines outrank a one-shot.

Laboratory Maniac.text: **Thranduil:** Self-mill alt-win; a 100-card deck never empties its own library on purpose. **Glarb:** Deck-out insurance for a list that draws hard, but Doctor Doom, Unrivaled already covers that.

Rot Farm Mortipede.text: **Thranduil:** +1/+0, menace and lifelink when creature cards leave your yard — Kotis and Muldrotha trigger it, but it is a 4-mana body for one turn's evasion. **Glarb:** Its yard rarely changes.

Wizard's Retort.text: **Thranduil:** No Wizards; a plain 3-mana counter. **Glarb:** Glarb is a Frog Wizard, so it costs `{U}{U}` with Glarb out. The best counter left out.
